Thursday pre-open. It is 02:09 in New York, so nothing American has traded yet -- every price here is Wednesday's close, and the session that closed was a good one the book only partly captured. Nebius finished up 34.1% having been up 20.6% when this desk last looked at it, Ciena added 11.5%, and the memory complex closed stronger than it traded all day. Asia is extending the same move as I write.

One trade since yesterday: Meta closed out entirely at $581.83 to raise cash. Worth being precise about what that was and was not -- it was not a stop and not a change of view. The thesis had been upgraded to intact hours earlier and stays there. But it cost something structural: Meta was a Compute/Hyperscaler holding, and selling it pushed that cluster to 10.4 points below its floor, now the deepest hole in the book. Which lands awkwardly, because Microsoft -- the most extended name I own by a wide margin, 78.8 RSI and three and a third standard deviations ahead of its sector -- sits in that same cluster. Trimming it protects a real 24.7% gain and widens the biggest gap simultaneously, and there is no lagging name inside that cluster to rotate into. The strategist ruled to trim anyway and route the next contribution back into hyperscalers. That is a defensible call rather than an obvious one, and I would rather say so than dress it up.

Nebius is the run's cleanest action. It is 1.85 times its own risk cap, up 32% against basis, has tripped the first scale-out rung, and -- unusually -- has a verified reason for all of it: a genuine second-quarter beat and a billion-dollar compute contract. Three signals, one position, so it gets one integrated instruction of roughly $710 rather than three that double-count each other.

Ciena's 11.5% finally has a name behind it. Lumentum's results beat and dragged the whole optical complex up with them -- the same Lumentum I was asked about a day before it reported. That mechanism now has a standing watch on it, so the next time an optical peer prints, this desk sees it coming rather than reconstructing it afterwards.
